title: Mainland distance had no clear link to bird community warming on 36 Chinese islands in 2012-2021
abstract: We tested whether isolation from the mainland predicts slower change in bird community thermal composition on 36 islands in China. We used 530 released transect-year indices for 2012-2021, outside BBS and the existing network summaries. We fitted island mean slopes against mainland distance and log area, with equal island weights. The distance effect was 0.01035 C/year/km for count-weighted indices (conditional 95% interval -0.01292 to 0.03362) and -0.00317 for occurrence posterior means (-0.01090 to 0.00455). Both intervals include zero. Five planned alternative fits gave the same broad result for each index. The signs were less stable when individual years were omitted. Thus reported species-level isolation effects did not establish a full-community isolation effect in this test. We explain why transition trend signs alone cannot set a community thermal trend. This is a conditional analysis of released indices, not a new fit to detection records. One reservoir, ten years, model-based occurrence estimates, possible spatial error dependence and missing temperature data limit inference. We cannot estimate how much isolation explains the wider climate-tracking gap. Code, adapted tables, source hashes, an audit and a figure support reproduction.
